title: Workers drain active commands safely during deployment
description:
As an operator, I want worker revisions to drain active commands before termination, so that routine deployments do not destroy long-running work.

Feature: Drain workers safely
  Scenario: A new worker revision is deployed while a command is running
    Given an old worker revision holds an active command lease
    When the deployment marks that revision as draining
    Then the old worker accepts no new commands
    And the active command may finish or transfer through the recovery protocol
    And the new revision accepts newly announced commands
    And deployment does not silently terminate the active command

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text:
Additional behavior for the service-loop slice:

Feature: Drain an always-on worker service
  Scenario: Drain begins while the worker is idle
    Given a worker service is waiting for commands
    When draining is requested
    Then it stops receiving new work and exits cleanly

  Scenario: Drain begins during command execution
    Given a worker service is executing a claimed command
    When draining is requested
    Then the active execution is allowed to settle
    And no additional command is received
    And the service exits after the active execution returns

  Scenario: Drain races with delivery receipt
    Given a delivery was received but execution has not started
    When draining is observed
    Then that delivery is released without execution
    And the service exits

comments.author: derek.norrbom
comments.text: Landed in develop through PR #537. The warm service loop stops intake on drain, settles active execution, releases deliveries caught by the drain race, and exits cleanly.
